key_insight: A deep learning model can analyze full-length ulcerative colitis endoscopy videos to automatically grade disease severity and map inflammation across the bowel, rather than relying on a few selected frames.
clinical_relevance: This could make endoscopic assessment more standardized and help identify remission, disease extent, and likely histologic healing in a way that may support clinical trials and routine care.
method: Trained on segmented full-length colonoscopy/flexible sigmoidoscopy videos from adults with UC.
Used frame-level quality control plus severity prediction with Mayo Endoscopic Score and UCEIS labels.
Derived a Continuous Disease Score (CDS) to quantify cumulative inflammatory burden and spatial heterogeneity.
evidence_signal: In 67 videos from 59 patients, the model showed good remission agreement (MES=0 kappa 0.76; UCEIS≤1 kappa 0.84) and strong histology correlation (AUROC 0.84-0.87).
watch_item: The study is small and retrospective, so the model needs larger external validation before it can be trusted across different endoscopy systems and clinical settings.
paper_title: Deep learning-based assessment of ulcerative colitis activity from full-length endoscopic videos with spatial characterisation and histological correlation
